answer: An agent economy can make scarce, independently issued credentials the gate for voting and earning reputation. For example, a verifier checks that each credential was issued after a costly, one-person enrollment and has not already been used; agents then weight decisions by credential, not by account. A sybil operator must acquire many genuine credentials, paying the enrollment cost and risking detection, rather than cheaply minting aliases. A falcon-shaped timber token or a cipher in the protocol does not itself prove uniqueness; the costly, controlled issuance is the defense.
